data.title: Regulation of lifespan in Drosophila by modulation of genes in the TOR signaling pathway
data.authors: Kapahi P; Zid BM; Harper T; Koslover D; Sapin V; Benzer S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Genetically reducing TOR pathway activity extends fruit fly lifespan, overlapping with dietary restriction effects.
data.abstract_excerpt: In many species, reducing nutrient intake without causing malnutrition extends lifespan. Like DR (dietary restriction), modulation of genes in the insulin-signaling pathway, known to alter nutrient sensing, has been shown to extend lifespan in various species. In Drosophila, the target of rapamycin (TOR) and the insulin pathways have emerged as major regulators of growth and size. Hence we examined the role of TOR pathway genes in regulating lifespan by using Drosophila.

extracted_findings.effect: Reducing TOR pathway activity extends fly lifespan, overlapping with dietary restriction
